touches.text: Every part is its own process: the bus, each shim, each device, the ground loop. Any one can be stopped and restarted alone while the rest run on. WHY: a self-modifying system needs that.
Messages sit in a SMALL buffer in memory. WHY: in memory is faster.

One bus per cairn instance, not per host. Each box runs its own bus, and the buses talk to one another, so a device always talks to the bus on its own box; together they are the instance's one bus. A device runs on one box; the other boxes reach it over the buses. No box needs a full set of devices. WHY: so the instance can run several heavy tasks at once across boxes.

Every box runs all the foundational things: a bus, a ground loop, the shims. They are the Cairn device's machines, and there is only one Cairn device: a singleton within the swarm, owning them on every box. WHY: Cairn is the system in aggregate, which is not the same thing as the host (6.6); a box is part of the host, and the swarm of boxes is still one Cairn.

There is no central supervisor. Each part starts what it needs by trying to use it: sending a message starts the bus if it is down, a message arriving wakes its shim, the shim wakes its device. Many very small supervisors, each one detect-and-start. WHY: a supervisor is one more thing to keep up, and the system must come up from any part that is touched.
The detect-and-start lives in one tool, the waker, and it sits inside connect: every client's connect is a wake attempt, so no caller can forget one. A probe watches and reports; the waker acts.

What the waker starts outlives whoever started it (detached, or through systemd-run --user, which gives it its own memory cap and log while still deciding nothing). Restarting a shim never takes down the bus it once woke.
CP4 Make everything suck less for everybody. Reduce friction for ALL affected beings: living beings, ecosystems, AIs. The terminal goal.
